title: Tightness of Kuperberg Algorithm 1's Bound
summary: Simulations of a one-pass variant match Algorithm 1's exponent and show a constant polynomial factor, but tightness and the correct factor for Algorithm 1 remain unproved.

formal_statement.body: For the hidden-shift problem, the original Kuperberg Algorithm 1 has a stated complexity bound for retrieving the last bit, while an improved one-pass Algorithm 2 has simulations whose exponent complexity matches that of Algorithm 1 and whose polynomial factor is constant. Determine rigorously whether the exponent in the original Algorithm 1 bound is tight and, if so, what the correct polynomial factor is, rather than relying on the indication that the exponent is probably tight but the polynomial factor is not. [S1]

scope.domain: Complexity analysis of Kuperberg hidden-shift algorithms.
parameters: Kuperberg Algorithms 1 and 2: the original and improved one-pass hidden-shift algorithms being compared
Exponent and polynomial factor: the two components of the last-bit retrieval complexity bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove whether the exponent in Algorithm 1's bound is tight and, if so, determine the correct polynomial factor.

citations.label: Hidden Shift Quantum Cryptanalysis and Implications

progress.summary: The source reports simulations for the improved one-pass Algorithm 2 that match Algorithm 1's exponent complexity and yield a constant polynomial factor. It presents this only as evidence that Algorithm 1's exponent is probably tight while its polynomial factor is not.
